title: Undertake development only with the development authorisation it needs
what: Get development approval (a permit) before carrying out development, or starting a use of land, that the planning scheme says needs one, and keep to the approval.

sources.title: Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 (SA)
sources.quote: (1) A person must not undertake development contrary to this Act. Maximum penalty: $120 000. Additional penalty. Default penalty: $500.

administration.who: Relevant authorities (councils, assessment panels, accredited professionals and the State Planning Commission, SA)

sources.title: Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 (SA)
sources.locator: s 7, words naming the body (found 18 Nov 2026)
sources.quote: the relevant authority must refuse to grant development authorisation in relation to the proposed development;

reach.condition: if its development needs a development authorisation

confidence_note: The Act's own words bar undertaking development contrary to the Act. Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of the official text, which is not itself official.

assessment.summary: Zoning and planning approvals limit how many homes can be built and where businesses can open. They push house prices far above the cost of building, add delays and paperwork, and can shelter existing businesses from new rivals. The Productivity Commission puts the cost of housing regulation at about 1% of GDP a year, mostly from zoning.

marks.reason: Zoning keeps house prices well above the cost of supply: a large distortion in the largest asset market.
Zoning and approvals limit the sites open to new businesses; the Harper Review found planning rules can favour incumbents.
Development approvals add paperwork, holding costs and delay to building homes and business premises.

assessment.confidence_note: No city estimate of the zoning premium was found for this jurisdiction; the marks rest on the Productivity Commission's national estimate and the common design of planning systems. Marks copied from the register item sa-planning-zoning so the two agree.
